headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being trafficked
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) reveals that men recruited for construction jobs were forced to fight in the Russian Army.
details: Twenty of 30 Bangladeshis allegedly recruited for the purpose of construction jobs in Russia have been killed after being forced to fight in the Russia-Ukraine war, according to the Special Response Battalion (SRB).
Additional DIG Asaduzzaman, commander of SRB-10, announced that 17 of the victims died in a drone strike on their first day at the front, while three others died later.
The case came to light following an investigation into a human trafficking case filed by the father of Rajon Hossain, a 21-year-old survivor who returned to Bangladesh on August 23.

Rajon was allegedly charged Tk 825,000 for a construction job. After arriving in Russia on May 7, he and others were forced into the Russian Army and given 21 days of training before being sent to the front.

A drone strike fractured Rajon's pelvis, leaving him unable to move his legs. He reportedly crawled nearly four kilometers to reach a camp and struggled for four days to get to a hospital before escaping.
Two alleged recruiters, Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher Lentu, were arrested on Tuesday. Investigators say the network operated through three companies: Jabal-e-Nur, RS International, and TS Group.
The trafficking network reportedly recruited young men from nine districts of Bangladesh, with assistance from collaborators in Russia and Kyrgyzstan.
The SRB states that while two returnees are recovering in Bangladesh, two others remain in a Moscow hospital and six are still on the battlefield.

headline_marked: Tk 3 lakh ransom demand after [[three schoolgirls go missing in Bandarban]]
headline: Tk 3 lakh ransom demand after three schoolgirls go missing in Bandarban
summary: A family received a video showing a person moving inside a sack as police search for the missing students from Lama upazila.
details: Three schoolgirls—two in class 7 and one in class 9—went missing from Lama upazila, Bandarban, while on their way to collect school registration cards.
One girl left home on October 11, followed by the other two. Since then, their families and police have been unable to contact them.
On Wednesday afternoon, a girl's parents received a video showing a person moving inside a sack, accompanied by a demand for Tk 3 lakh in ransom.
Lama Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Kaisar Hamid confirmed the video and the ransom demand, stating that operations are ongoing to rescue the girls.
Police investigations found that the girls were last traced to neighboring Chakaria upazila in Cox's Bazar, and they may have traveled further toward Cox's Bazar town or Ramu.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operations) Jinia Chakma noted that the video may have been sent by an extortionist gang that exploits families' distress over missing children.
The disappearance has caused significant tension and concern among residents of the Yangsha-Anghlari Para area in Fasiakhali union.
Police are continuing their search and rescue efforts, though they stated it is too early to draw final conclusions until the girls are found.
